clue.text: Method's restraining bad actor's interchanges

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the first word's letters hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: a recipe is a method for cooking, and the possessive adds S

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of the word that follows are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: the word as printed, before its possessive

explanation.surface: An unruly performer's exchanges are kept in check by a theatrical method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Method' suggests acting technique, fitting the actor, but it is a cookery recipe. The 's of actor's reads as 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reciprocate is to give in return, so the verb means makes mutual exchanges.

clue.text: Pieces of Cheddar are bitten eating this?

definitions.text: Pieces of Cheddar are bitten eating this?

indicators.note: only parts of these words are used, so the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A question about what dish has chunks of cheese being nibbled.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of Cheddar, all of 'are' and the start of bitten; the whole clue also describes eating cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, so Cheddar is eaten in it.

clue.text: Interior's covering explosive fuses

indicators.note: one piece covers the other, so it goes around it

parts.note: the core is the interior, and the possessive adds S
HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive

explanation.surface: A bomb's inner casing wraps around its fuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuses' looks like a noun for detonators but is the verb: sticks together.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together as one, a synonym of fuse as a verb.

clue.text: Long drink contains very soft fruit

parts.note: to long for is to pine

indicators.note: the drink word holds the musical letters inside it

parts.note: ale is a drink
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A tall glass holds some gentle fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long drink' looks like one phrase, but Long is the verb PINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pineapple is a tropical fruit, an example of the category.

clue.text: Old worked keeping in good heart, say

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the letter for good goes inside

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means worked or operated

explanation.surface: An elderly person worked to stay healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks heart as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is one example of a bodily organ, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Fat detective assuming a position

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the pose phrase takes the detective inside

parts.note: a pose is a position, with A as printed
DI is the abbreviation for detective inspector

explanation.surface: A portly police detective strikes a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means fatty, as in adipose tissue, the body's fat store.

clue.text: Trouble filling hospital department's needs

indicators.note: one piece fills the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital, plus the possessive S
to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you

explanation.surface: A problem fills up a hospital unit's requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: If something entails a thing it requires it, so the verb means necessitates.

clue.text: For each upset select man changing substitutes

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person

indicators.note: changing signals that these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: For each awkward selection, a team official makes changes to the subs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses PER to REP; 'changing' rearranges SELECTMAN to LACEMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Substitutes are people or things put in place of others, the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Eastern sculpture, perhaps, bird in clay

parts.note: sculpture is an example of art, hence perhaps
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: An oriental statue of a bird modelled in clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthenware is pottery made of fired clay, so the adjective means made of baked earth or clay.

clue.text: Flash last of Big Issue

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: issue means offspring, and a litter is a brood of young animals

explanation.surface: A flashy final edition of the Big Issue, the magazine sold by homeless vendors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Issue is a British street magazine; here Issue means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter is showy sparkle, the noun sense of flash as dazzle.

clue.text: Queen on the up, meaning distribute record

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
the gist is the meaning
to ration is to share out or distribute

explanation.surface: The monarch, rising in fortune, means to hand out an official record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' reverses ER to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A registration is an entry in an official list, a formal record.

clue.text: Country beginning to launch airline

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is its first letter

parts.note: Iberia is the Spanish national airline

explanation.surface: A nation is starting up its own airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African country, an example of the category.

clue.text: Catching nothing with snooping around

indicators.note: the prying word goes around the zero, holding it inside

parts.note: nosing about is snooping
O, zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone prying about catches nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Noosing means snaring in a looped rope, a way of catching.

clue.text: Pierced one's skin

parts.note: pierced in the sense of cut into
I is the Roman numeral one, and the possessive gives S

explanation.surface: Someone's skin has been punctured.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical term for the skin, the dermis plus epidermis.

clue.text: Crew's seizing stern of pirate ship and holds

indicators.note: to seize is to grab hold of, so the crew word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a posse is a band or crew, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so the final letter of the next word

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A gang grabs the back of a pirate vessel and keeps it.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess is to own or have, so the verb matches holds as in holds property.

clue.text: One pays to purchase useless underwear article

indicators.note: purchase also means a grip, so the payer takes hold of the other letters

parts.note: a spender is one who pays
US is crossword shorthand for unserviceable, useless

explanation.surface: A shopper pays for some worthless lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying, but here it means a grip or hold, which signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is a strap that holds up stockings, an item of underwear.

clue.text: Compact cars brief condensed for cabinet members

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: terse means condensed or concise

explanation.surface: Small cars made shorter for government officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts TERSE to TERS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabinet members in government are senior ministers heading departments.

clue.text: Fertiliser can's rising cost

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tin is a can
a rate is a cost or charge

explanation.surface: The price of a tin of fertiliser is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses TIN to NIT; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are nitrogen salts widely spread on fields as plant fertiliser.

clue.text: One posts squad leader on watch

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the first letter of the word

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch

explanation.surface: A team captain is put on guard duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places S above TICKER in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill sticker is one who posts notices, and a label that is stuck up is posted.

clue.text: Initially earnest, agog, great enthusiasm rising

definitions.text: Initially earnest, agog, great enthusiasm rising

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A description of someone keen and agog, their enthusiasm swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the five words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest, agog and full of enthusiasm describe keenness, the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Competitor in event ran tiredly

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An athlete in a race ran wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who enters a contest, so a competitor.

clue.text: Beauty shown by heartless girl French love

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: amour is French for love

explanation.surface: Beauty displayed by a cold-hearted girl in a French romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring attractiveness, a synonym of beauty.

clue.text: Idiots rolling in, dancing twist

indicators.note: rolling turns the little word over so its letters change order
dancing moves the letters of the dance name around

explanation.surface: Fools come rolling in to do the twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' turns IN to NI; 'dancing' rearranges TWIST to TWITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitwits and idiots are both foolish people, plural synonyms.

clue.text: Slump includes credit squeeze

indicators.note: the first word takes in the abbreviation

parts.note: to sag is to slump
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: An economic slump brings a credit squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit squeeze' reads as one phrase but splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrag is to wring the neck of, so to throttle or squeeze.

clue.text: Concentrate more facing court

parts.note: extra means more, additional

explanation.surface: Pay more attention when appearing before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a concentrated preparation, like vanilla essence, so a concentrate.

clue.text: One obsessively follows speech in sermon, half cut

indicators.note: the talk word goes inside the shortened sermon
cutting the word in half keeps its first three letters

parts.note: a talk is a speech

explanation.surface: A preacher's sermon is cut short by a fixated follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' keeps the first half of the six-letter word; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker is someone who persistently and obsessively pursues another person.

clue.text: Return tennis stroke with assistance before love game

indicators.note: return means turn back, so the two words read backwards

parts.note: a lob is a high tennis shot
aid is assistance
love is zero in tennis, and O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Hitting a tennis return, with help, before a love game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' reverses LOBAID to DIABOL, placed before O.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling toy and the game of spinning it on a string.

clue.text: Freezing environment in wild for rare tiger

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An icy habitat in the wild for a rare tiger, like the Siberian.
explanation.definitionFit: A fridge keeps its contents cold, a chilled space, hence a freezing environment.
